run.name: 13-parallax-depth
run.finalText:
I built the parallax shot as a 10-layer, 8-second scene with a slow push-in and a pan to the right. I checked the frames and tweaked the sky tint, haze and sun. After the last change, which moved the sun to the right so the title no longer touches it, I did not re-render.

- **Depth layers:** Sky (with a Sky Top tint) and Sun Glow sit at the back. In front of them, in order, are Far Mountains, Mid Hills, Near Trees and Foreground Grass.
- **Parallax:** Over the 8 seconds, the farther layers pan and scale less than the near ones.
  - Far Mountains: about 35px of pan and 105% scale.
  - Mid Hills: about 90px and 112%.
  - Near Trees: about 190px and 122%.
  - Foreground Grass: about 360px and 145%.
  - The sky and sun barely move.
- **Atmospheric haze:** The far layers use lighter, lower-contrast colours (pale blue-grey for the mountains, mid blue-grey for the hills). Two soft haze bands, Haze Far and Haze Near, move with the layers they sit behind.
- **Title:** "Into the Quiet" sits in the stack between Mid Hills and Near Trees. It fades in from 2.5s to 4.2s and moves with a depth between the hills and trees.

I could only fake the sky gradient with two overlapping rectangles, since layers take a single fill colour. If you want it smoother, I can add a few more bands. I can also make the push stronger or change the title timing.

items.text: parallax: ≥3 layers moving at clearly different speeds
gradient sky or haze (gradient paint or translucent layers)
title sits between hills and trees in the layer order
